checkedAlternates.risk: Diagrams often draw an oval as a rounded rectangle, which can read as a four-sided shape.
checkedAlternates.resolution: An oval has no straight sides at all, so the side count can only place it with the circle.

checkedAlternates.risk: Trapezoid is the least familiar quadrilateral name; a player unsure of the shape may assume more sides.
checkedAlternates.resolution: A trapezoid has exactly four sides, so it sits with the other quadrilaterals.

checkedAlternates.risk: The single-item row is the easiest slot to misassign, and a square drawn on a diagonal can read as two triangles.
checkedAlternates.resolution: Three sides is the only side count in the puzzle with one representative, so the solo row is forced once the four-sided group is filled.

authorReview.notes: The dimension is countable rather than interpretive, which is why this one opens the batch: it is the safest of the ten.

blindPlaytest.notes: Watch whether testers count the sides at all or pattern-match on shape names.
